summary.headline: Borosil Renewables FY26 standalone sales rose 38% to INR1,534.83 crore and EBITDA margin hit 32% on higher solar glass realisations.
summary.overview: Q4 FY26 standalone sales were INR437.62 crore (up ~34% YoY, a record quarter) with EBITDA of INR144.61 crore at 33% of sales, helped by average ex-factory realisation of INR150.2/mm and about 15% higher volumes. Management attributed roughly half the quarterly sales jump to Ind AS revenue recognition timing (about 6% of Q4 sales), and said the run-rate is nearer INR400-410 crore a quarter. Fuel surcharges passed to customers during the West Asia-driven gas price spike had negligible net impact on realisation (under INR1/mm). The company wrote off its German exposure (Geosphere and GMB) with no additional P&L loss, as a provision was already made in Q1 FY26. Management also announced a rooftop solar branded-products venture, a 600 TPD furnace expansion targeted for Q4 FY27, and an enabling resolution to raise up to INR750 crore in equity.

segments.name: Solar glass (standalone, Bharuch)
segments.commentary: FY26 sales INR1,534.83 crore with EBITDA margin 32%; Q4 volumes up 15% YoY and 14% QoQ, with production run at full capacity and no curtailment during the West Asia disruption.

segments.name: Overseas subsidiaries (Germany)
segments.commentary: Q4 FY26 overseas net revenue INR2.3 crore and EBITDA INR0.82 crore, versus INR3.96 crore and INR1.90 crore in the prior quarter; German production shut from July 2025 and exposure to Geosphere and GMB written off.

segments.name: Rooftop solar (new division)
segments.commentary: Early-stage branded rooftop solutions business sourcing modules, inverters and batteries from outside vendors; first sales booked in March 2026, with a first-year target of about INR75 crore and expected initial EBITDA margin below 10%.

guidance_outlook: Management sees 30-33% EBITDA margin as achievable on a normal basis, barring unforeseen circumstances.
Run-rate quarterly sales of about INR400-410 crore after the roughly 6% Ind AS timing benefit in Q4 falls away.

600 TPD of new capacity (two 300 TPD furnaces) targeted for production within FY27; management said the first furnace is on track for around January 2027 and that sales contribution should come from Q1 FY28, with some sales possible in FY27.
Tax rate expected around 21% of PBT, with minimal cash tax while INR950 crore of expansion capex is capitalised.
SG1 and SG2 furnace rebuild capex of about INR100 crore expected in the next calendar year.
Customs notification for continuation of countervailing duty on Malaysian solar glass expected before the current duty expires on 6-8 June 2026.
capex_capacity: Expansion of 600 TPD (two 300 TPD furnaces) at the existing location is in full swing; nearly all orders placed and building construction on plan, taking capacity from about 1,000 TPD to about 1,600 TPD (around 60% uplift).
Management cited INR950 crore of capitalisation planned in the current financial year.

Domestic solar glass capacity is about 2,600 TPD (about 18 GW); about 33 GW of further capacity is expected by March 2027, mostly captive, taking the domestic total to about 51 GW against demand of about 65 GW.
Rooftop business: no capex for 1-1.5 years; the company may consider inverter assembly after 6-8 months to a year, but not module manufacturing.
Board approved an enabling resolution to raise equity up to INR750 crore, subject to shareholder approval; management said there are no current plans to raise capital.
demand_pricing: Realisation held near INR150/mm; management said pass-through of gas and fuel cost added less than INR1/mm, and that the price is tied to the landed cost of Chinese imports and near peak levels, with rupee depreciation providing only limited headroom.
Domestic solar installations were 44.6 GW in FY26 versus 23.8 GW in FY25, implying about 60-62 GW of glass consumption; imports still supply about 70% of demand.
ALMM-II (domestic solar cells) effective June 2026; solar cell capacity at 30 GW, expected to reach 75 GW by FY-end; ALMM-III for ingots and wafers from June 2028.

Indonesian Chinese-owned plant (about 1,500 TPD) has entered the market but has made limited impact so far; the Turkish producer's exports face high freight costs; the UAE plant is blocked by Strait of Hormuz conditions.
Export demand is low in major markets; the US may grow as customers seek non-Chinese origin glass, and Europe has niche demand for greenhouses and flat-plate collectors.

Cost pressure from oil-linked inputs is so far modest; vendors are seeking pass-through and the company is negotiating; gas quantities are secured under medium- and short-term contracts, but spot prices are high.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the INR150/mm realisation comes from fuel pass-through, and what would it be without it?
qa_highlights.answer: Ashok Jain said the pass-through contributed less than INR1/mm, about INR0.70-0.75, and a similar increase is visible in net realisation between Q3 and Q4.

qa_highlights.question: Will realisation or margins come under pressure as new domestic capacity arrives?
qa_highlights.answer: Management sees no pressure for domestic producers; most upcoming capacity is captive, demand exceeds the 51 GW expected capacity, and Indonesian imports are not yet a price threat.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the 13-15% sequential sales growth with flat realisation?
qa_highlights.answer: Roughly half was production gain (about 7%) and half was Ind AS timing: in-transit sales were lower at the end of Q3 and so were recognised in Q4, with the sales base reset to about INR400-410 crore a quarter.

qa_highlights.question: Is gas supply secure given the West Asia crisis?
qa_highlights.answer: Quantities are broadly secured under medium- and short-term contracts; the government gas cut is based on the past six-month average, and the rest is bought at market-related prices, so price rather than volume is the constraint.

qa_highlights.question: What is the rooftop solar roadmap, capex and margin profile?
qa_highlights.answer: No capex for 1-1.5 years; modules, inverters and batteries will be outsourced; first-year target is about INR75 crore, with margins expected below 10% initially and little or no profit in year one; working capital is kept low by negotiating terms.

qa_highlights.question: Will the furnace expansion commissioning timeline hold, and what does it do to margins?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said timing is as currently planned (first furnace around January 2027), with sales from Q1 FY28; operating leverage and higher yield are expected, but management did not commit to a specific margin uplift.

qa_highlights.question: What is the outlook for depreciation and tax?
qa_highlights.answer: Depreciation has fallen because older SG1 and SG2 assets are fully depreciated; current charge mainly reflects the 2023 expansion. Tax is around 21% of PBT, with deferred tax at a similar rate.

risks_watch: CVD on Malaysian solar glass expires 6-8 June 2026; a delayed or diluted notification would affect pricing.
Fuel surcharge and gas price volatility from the West Asia conflict; management said the Q1 FY27 reset depends on the 30 June stock-take.
Ind AS timing effects could make quarterly sales lumpy; management flagged the INR400-410 crore run-rate as the base case.
Indonesian Chinese-owned capacity could pressure prices; management suggested BIS and quality-control measures as a mitigant.
Rooftop business faces competition from Tata Power, Havells and Luminous, and early margins are guided below 10%.
Furnace commissioning slippage (first furnace January 2027 target) and the planned INR100 crore SG1/SG2 rebuild capex.
Export demand remains weak in Europe; freight costs are high because of Red Sea and Hormuz disruptions.
summary.management_tone: Confident on the domestic demand-supply gap and pricing, but cautious on the sustainability of Q4 sales, which management explicitly said were inflated by Ind AS timing. Management was evasive on expansion beyond the 600 TPD project, and on furnace timing beyond a 'we'll see' at the Q2 call. Tone on the rooftop venture was enthusiastic, with the chairman openly saying margins would be far lower.

key_quotes: The rise in selling prices has been possible only after the government's positive approach by levying antidumping duties on solar glass imports from China and Vietnam in December 2024.
I'm happy to say that the rise in fuel cost has not so far made any impact on our margins.
Initially, we may expect less than 10%, just to give you a number.
So, on a run rate basis, if you want to look at maybe INR400 crores or thereabouts is a good -- INR400 crores, INR410 crores is a good amount to look at.
I would be very surprised if it is a similar line. It could be a lot lower than this.

adds.what: 600 TPD (two 300 TPD furnaces) new solar glass capacity at existing Bharuch location, taking capacity from ~1,000 TPD to ~1,600 TPD

growth.why: Management guides 30-33% EBITDA margin as achievable and run-rate sales of INR400-410 crore a quarter (below the Q4 record, which included ~6% Ind AS timing benefit); 600 TPD furnace expansion (~60% capacity uplift, INR950 crore capitalisation) is nearly all ordered and targeted for production within FY27, but the first furnace is ~Jan 2027 with meaningful sales from Q1 FY28.
